headline: Single-cell and harmonized public data resolve tumor clones, copy number and ecDNA
label: Computational Cancer Genomics Frameworks
summary: Single-cell RNA-seq inference and harmonized copy number resources now allow tumor cell and ecDNA characterization.
synthesis: The common thread is extracting tumor-intrinsic genomic information from data already available, either through harmonized resources or from transcriptomic readouts. PanCNV-Explorer consolidates copy number variation data across 33 cancer types, cell lines and healthy cohorts into a unified, browsable database. The two single-cell items instead infer genomic features from scRNA-seq expression. SCANBIT pools transcriptionally similar clusters to call SNVs and uses bootstrapped hierarchical clustering to identify tumor cell populations. ecSingle infers oncogene-carrying extrachromosomal DNA from allelic imbalance and outlier expression, resolving ecDNA clonal evolution and selection. What is new is the application of scRNA-seq readouts to call SNVs and infer ecDNA, extending genomic inference to individual tumor cells. The database item addresses infrastructure, while the single-cell items address inference.
